name: Ospeli command layer
description: Every action in the Ospeli app is one of these commands. People and agents run the same commands. Synthetic data only in this build.
rules: People decide, Ospeli suggests: an agent may read, and its write commands become proposals that wait for a person.

A proposal is checked before it is queued: the bed, patient, work order or map must exist and be in a state that allows the action, or the call is refused (not-found or conflict). The same call again returns the proposal already waiting (existing: true). One agent may have one open proposal per command for a bed or work order, and at most 20 proposals waiting in all; 20 is an example setting, not a standard.
Agent access is off by default, for the hospital and for each ward (ospeli_agents_set_access, people only).

Only agents on the site's list may call (ospeli_agents_add, people only): each has one role, its wards and an end date of 90 days at most. An agent that is not listed, is past its end date or claims another role is refused. Agents are named, not verified: the browser app has no secret keys; the first version of the site server gives each agent one.
Anyone on site can stop every agent at once (ospeli_agents_stop_all); only the operations manager or chief operating officer can switch agents on again.
Agent reads, proposals and refusals made through window.ospeli.run are designed to be recorded in the audit trail with actor type "agent", the agent name and the role it acts for.

In the browser app these rules are kept by the app's own code and are not a security boundary: a script running in the page can load the app's modules and act as a person, and the trail would then record a person. The first version of the site server (tools/ospeli-server/, run on a site's own computer) checks agent keys and records every call made with a key as that agent, never as a person. A person acts at the server's own window, or from a phone or laptop connected there with a one-time code (recorded as a person in a role from that device, not as a named person); named sign-in is not built yet.
Nothing leaves the site: commands run on this device or the hospital's own server, never through a cloud relay.

howToCall.browser: window.ospeli.commands(), window.ospeli.describe(name), await window.ospeli.run(name, input, { agent: "your-agent-name", role: "bed-manager" }). Add dryRun: true to rehearse a call: every check runs and nothing is read, queued or changed. The options are agent, role and dryRun; any other option is refused (invalid-input) and nothing runs.
howToCall.examples: Each command has an example input. The ids in it are examples. Where example.needs is present, the example runs only once that is in place (a map exists, a bed is in the named state, a proposal is waiting); the line names the read that finds a real id. An example with no needs line runs as written on the example hospital.
howToCall.names: Command names are ospeli_<module>_<action>. The dotted names used before 12 Nov 2026 still work in this build; each is listed as deprecatedName. The audit trail and the proposal queue always record the new name. Use the new names.
howToCall.lists: List reads take a limit and return total and truncated; most take format: "short". Start with the task-shaped reads: ospeli_beds_find_free, ospeli_workorders_list (overdue, locationId) and ospeli_maps_summary.
howToCall.errors: A refused call throws an error with .code: invalid-input, unknown-command, forbidden, not-found, conflict or agents-off. agents-off means only that agent access is switched off, for the hospital or for that ward. forbidden covers the rest: a people-only command (a person does it on screen), an agent that is not on the site's list or is past its end date, or a role that cannot run the command. A missing input is read as {}; an input that is not a JSON object is invalid-input.

commands.name: ospeli_beds_find_free
commands.summary: Find a free bed for a patient who is waiting: the beds that are available now (the ward the patient was requested for first), and who has waited longest. To hold a bed, a person runs ospeli_beds_allocate (an agent's allocate becomes a proposal). Read-only.

commands.name: ospeli_transfers_board
commands.summary: The dispatch board in one call: journeys waiting for a vehicle (in the order they are needed: a booked time, or when an as-soon-as-possible request was made), journeys with a vehicle, every vehicle (free, on a job or off the road; crewed this shift or not; its last daily check), the four measures with their definitions and sources, and the guide's suggestions with their reasons and basis (empty while the guide is off). Also the pick lists, places and bookable times. Measures journeys and vehicles, never drivers. Read-only.
commands.agentBehaviour: runs and is audited as an agent read

days.description: The period for the measures: the last this many days. Default 7.

format.description: short: no pick lists, places or definitions. detailed (default): the measures with definitions, plus pick lists, places and bookable times.

limit.description: At most this many journeys in each list. Default 50, 500 at most. "total" and "truncated" in the answer say if there are more.

synthetic.description: True while the data on this device is synthetic.

open.description: Journeys with a vehicle, not yet handed over.

value.description: null when nothing was counted in the period.

action.description: The first command a person may run to follow it; null: advice only. actions lists them all. A fault report needs a priority the person picks.

total.description: How many there are in all, before the limit.

truncated.description: True when the limit cut the list short. Narrow the filters or raise the limit.

commands.name: ospeli_transfers_request
commands.summary: Book a journey in a vehicle: from a ward or department, to one of our sites or an outside category (never a name or an address), as soon as possible or for a booked time, with how the patient travels, who escorts them and the equipment, all picked from lists. No typed text and no clinical notes. The ward sets mobility and escort; Ospeli records the pick. A move on foot inside a site is a Cleaning and transport job instead. The same journey sent twice within two minutes is one booking unless "again" is true (a second patient). An agent's call becomes a proposal for a person.
commands.agentBehaviour: recorded as a proposal for a person to accept or decline; nothing changes until they do

type.description: What kind of journey. One of: discharge (Discharge), between-sites (Between our sites), to-provider (To another provider), appointment (Appointment).

fromPlace.description: The ward or department the patient leaves from, for example ward-a1.

toSite.description: One of our sites, for example site-north. Give this or toOutside.

toOutside.description: An outside destination as a category, never a name or address. Give this or toSite. One of: other-hospital (Another hospital), care-home (Care home), hospice (Hospice), home (Home (no address kept here)), other (Somewhere else).

needed.description: asap: as soon as possible (the wait starts now). booked: at bookedFor.

bookedFor.description: For a booked journey: when the patient must leave, up to seven days ahead.

mobility.description: How the patient travels, as the ward set it. One of: walks (Walks (may need a hand)), wheelchair (Wheelchair), stretcher (Stretcher), two-crew (Needs two crew to move), special (Special handling: agree with the coordinator).

escort.description: Who travels with the patient, as the ward set it. One of: none (No escort), carer (Relative or carer), nurse (Nurse or nursing assistant), clinician (Doctor or other clinician).

equipment.description: What must travel. ["none"] for nothing. One or more of: none, oxygen, pump, wide, aids, belongings.

bayMove.description: true when a move to the vehicle bay is already asked for in Cleaning and transport. This command does not ask for it.

again.description: true to book a second, identical journey (another patient) within two minutes of the first.

transferId.description: A transfer id, for example trf-00012 (ospeli_transfers_board lists them).
